queries: Matt Shumer "Something Big Is Happening" post

sources_considered.why: Primary text of the essay under review.
Republication. The original essay was enough.

evidence_items.locator: section 'I know this is real because it happened to me first', paragraph 4

receipt.public_excerpt: I tell the AI what I want, walk away from my computer for four hours, and come back to find the work done. Done well, done better than I would have done it myself, with no corrections needed.

evidence_items.explanation: This is the error-free-output claim Marcus refers to. Its only support is Shumer's own experience, not data.

evidence_items.locator: section 'I know this is real because it happened to me first', paragraph 5

receipt.public_excerpt: Only once it has decided the app meets its own standards does it come back to me and say: "It's ready for you to test." And when I test it, it's usually perfect.

evidence_items.explanation: Shumer's whole-app example is an anecdote ('what my Monday looked like'), with no error rates or test data.

evidence_items.locator: section 'What this means for your job', Software engineering paragraph

receipt.public_excerpt: A year ago, AI could barely write a few lines of code without errors. Now it writes hundreds of thousands of lines that work correctly.

evidence_items.explanation: A second correctness claim, again with no cited data or source.

evidence_items.locator: section 'How fast this is actually moving', paragraph 8

receipt.public_excerpt: There's an organization called METR that actually measures this with data. They track the length of real-world tasks (measured by how long they take a human expert) that a model can complete successfully end-to-end without human help.

evidence_items.explanation: This is the only data Shumer cites. It measures task length, does not state the 50% success criterion, and does not measure error-free app building.

unresolved_gaps: Shumer's essay may have been edited after publication. The text read on the evaluation date shows no data on error-free apps.
